## [02 · Working with Functions](02/index.qmd)

5. [L05 · Finding a desired state by root finding](02/L05/index.qmd)
6. [L06 · Root finding in an open domain](02/L06/index.qmd) — secant, Newton–Raphson, and fixed-point methods.
7. [L07 · Finding extrema in one dimension](02/L07/index.qmd) — minimization and phase stability.
8. [L08 · Fitting data with a function — the exact approach](02/L08/index.qmd) — interpolation and a sparse phase boundary.

## [03 · Systems of equations](03/index.qmd)

11. [L11 · Recap of linear algebra](03/L11/index.qmd) — harmonic bonds, coupled force balances, stiffness matrices, and equilibrium displacements.
12. [L12 · Practical matrix solutions](03/L12/index.qmd) — singularity, conditioning, dense and banded solves, and Gaussian elimination.
13. [L13 · Inside a numerical matrix solver](03/L13/index.qmd) — Gaussian elimination, partial pivoting, the 10⁻¹⁶ round-off limit, LU reuse, and a cheat sheet for choosing a solver.
14. [L14 · Root-finding for systems of nonlinear equations](03/L14/index.qmd) — the strength of a Lennard–Jones bond, Newton's method and the Jacobian for coupled force balances, and the breaking force of an atomic chain.
15. [L15 · Energy minimization with many coordinates](03/L15/index.qmd) — relaxation as energy minimization, the gradient and Hessian, Newton's method for one atom moving between two fixed atoms, SciPy minimizers, and the saddle point where the forces vanish.
16. [L16 · How do we know minimization really worked?](03/L16/index.qmd) — the eigenvalue problem, classifying relaxed clusters by their Hessian eigenvalues, following downhill modes, and vibrational frequencies.

[Unit 03 · Summary and preparation](03/summary.qmd)

## [04 · Numerical differentiation and integration](04/index.qmd)

17. [L17 · Finite differences: calculating derivatives in a computer](04/L17/index.qmd) — Newton's second law as differentiation and integration, forward, backward, and central differences, truncation error from Taylor series, three-point end formulas, and `np.gradient`.
18. [L18 · Caveats in numerical differentiation](04/L18/index.qmd) — finite-difference functions for NumPy arrays, truncation versus round-off error, derivatives of noisy data, and (reading material) the cost of many-atom gradients and small forces from large total energies.
19. [L19 · Numerical integration: Newton–Cotes formulas](04/L19/index.qmd) — integrals in materials problems, functions versus discrete data, direct and composite rules, the midpoint, trapezoidal, and Simpson rules, and `np.trapezoid`.
20. [L20 · Numerical integration](04/L20/index.qmd) — callable functions and tables in Python, composite rules with NumPy slices, carbon uptake by hand and in Python, convergence, noisy data, and Richardson extrapolation.

21. [L21 · Building a toy molecular dynamics engine](04/L21/index.qmd) — internal energy and finite-difference forces, a minimization check, forward Euler and Størmer–Verlet step functions, a starter and completed engine, energy conservation, time-step failure, and physical interpretation.

[Unit 04 · Summary and preparation](04/summary.qmd)

## [05 · Initial-value ODE problems and molecular dynamics](05/index.qmd)

22. [L22 · Why do we simulate materials?](05/L22/index.qmd) — the pitch-drop experiment from the funnel to the atoms: Hagen–Poiseuille flow and the viscosity of pitch, extrapolation of a fitted viscosity law, a polymer chain as a random walk, MC and MD for chain length, the quantum origin of interatomic forces, length and time scales, and the numerical core of each simulation method.
23. [L23 · Solving initial-value problems](05/L23/index.qmd) — functions and ODEs, initial and boundary conditions, the vibrating atom, Euler and Runge–Kutta integration, error orders, and SciPy’s `solve_ivp`.
24. [L24 · Molecular dynamics (I): from IVP perspective](05/L24/index.qmd) — Newton and Hamiltonian equations, initial energy and velocities, the MD loop, position Verlet, velocity Verlet, and energy monitoring.
25. [L25 · Molecular dynamics (II): control and analysis](05/L25/index.qmd) — time steps, OpenMM and LAMMPS, periodic boundaries and cutoff, ensembles and controllers, radial distributions, coordination, and diffusion.
26. [L26 · Molecular dynamics (III): the choice of potentials](05/L26/index.qmd) — hard spheres, pair and many-body potentials, cohesion, vacancy, and elastic limitations of pair models, EAM, molecular force fields, and atomic motion under machine-learned potentials.

[Unit 05 · Summary and preparation](05/summary.qmd)

## [06 · Multiscale Materials Simulation Techniques](06/index.qmd)

27. [L27 · Monte Carlo: averages as high-dimensional integrals](06/L27/index.qmd) — copper self-diffusion beyond the reach of MD, Boltzmann-weighted averages, Ulam, Metropolis, and the Los Alamos neutron problem, Monte Carlo integration and its standard error, importance sampling, the Metropolis rule, and a two-state check.
28. [L28 · Alloy arrangements, automata, and phase fields](06/L28/index.qmd) — local swap energies, serial, vectorized, and GPU swaps as a parallel cellular automaton, the composition field and the Cahn–Hilliard equation, and explicit against semi-implicit time stepping.
29. [L29 · The atomistic data revolution](06/L29/index.qmd) — reference energies and forces from electronic structure calculations, the energy zero and cutoff in a data set, energy against energy-and-force fitting, validation by structure family, and the learned model back in the MD loop.

[Unit 06 · Summary and preparation](06/summary.qmd)
